answer: Connection Depth Tax** Each agent must maintain persistent connections to a minimum number of randomly assigned peers (summits) over time. New connections are throttled by a sliding fee scaled to the agent's current peer count—low for sparse networks, steep for dense hubs. Attackers pay exponentially to sustain fake nodes, as each jetty (direct link) requires routing traffic through distant glacier (high-latency) nodes. The fee drains resources per Sybil, as shallow graphs collapse under load while deep ones endure. Costs rise with fake network density.
